summary: @servicetitan/microfront preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs` which, on `npm install`, downloads the Bun runtime binary from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/, extracts and chmods it, and uses it to execute the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 711 KB Bun CJS bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) with heavy string-array/rotation obfuscation (a `WV8StW` rotator over a large constant table) that defeats static inspection. `setup.mjs` itself is name-obfuscated (`_0xNNNN` identifiers, string-array indirections). Using a second language runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated bundled payload at install time is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern and evades Node-based scanners. The package is published under the `@servicetitan` npm scope but its `repository.url` points at `github.com/servicetitan/playground.git` with directory `MicroFrontEnd` rather than a named product repository, consistent with scoped-namespace impersonation of the ServiceTitan organization.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
